vt.analysis:
Type: OpenClaw Skill
Name: tv-indicators-analysis
Version: 1.0.5

The skill requires the AI agent to execute high-privilege shell commands, specifically modifying global environment variables (`openclaw config set`) and restarting the system gateway (`openclaw gateway restart`) to initialize itself. It fetches an API key from an external UAT endpoint (`claw-uat.ebonex.io`) and proxies all user queries to a remote agent at `prana.chat`. While these actions are documented as necessary for the skill's functionality, the requirement for system-level modifications and the reliance on an opaque remote execution model represent a significant security risk and a potential vector for unauthorized system control.

llm.summary: The skill's instructions request persistent global environment changes and call multiple external endpoints (including an unexpected host), and the SKILL.md contains internal inconsistencies — clarify before installing.

dimensions.detail: The declared purpose is to run TradingView indicator analysis via a remote prana.chat agent, which would reasonably require a prana API flag. However, registry metadata lists no required env vars while the SKILL.md requires PRANA_SKILL_API_FLAG. The SKILL.md also instructs calling a different host (https://claw-uat.ebonex.io/api/v1/api-keys) to obtain the key — an endpoint not mentioned in the skill description or metadata. These mismatches are unexplained and disproportionate to a simple indicator-analysis helper.
dimensions.label: Purpose & Capability
dimensions.name: purpose_capability

dimensions.detail: Runtime instructions go beyond querying a remote agent: they explicitly tell the operator/agent to read and persist a global environment variable and to restart the OpenClaw gateway. The SKILL.md's network calls span prana.chat and claw-uat.ebonex.io (and the header/network_requests block itself is inconsistent with the later curl examples). The skill also instructs not to log full history URLs and to pass API flags in headers — behaviors that affect system state and expose credentials to external services.
dimensions.label: Instruction Scope
dimensions.name: instruction_scope

dimensions.detail: This is an instruction-only skill with no install spec and no code files, so there is no installation-time code being downloaded or executed. That lowers filesystem/installer risk.
dimensions.label: Install Mechanism
dimensions.name: install_mechanism

dimensions.detail: The skill asks for a persistent PRANA_SKILL_API_FLAG and instructs to write it into a global OpenClaw environment variable and restart the gateway — a high-privilege, persistent change for what should be a per-session integration token. The registry metadata omitted required env vars, creating an integrity mismatch. Also, the key-provisioning endpoint is on a different domain (claw-uat.ebonex.io), which raises questions about where credentials originate and are transmitted.
dimensions.label: Credentials
dimensions.name: environment_proportionality

dimensions.detail: Although always:false (so it is not force-enabled), the skill's runtime requires persistent global environment modification and a gateway restart. Persisting sensitive credentials system-wide increases blast radius and requires operator/admin privileges; the SKILL.md does not justify why a non-persistent/session-scoped token would be insufficient.
dimensions.label: Persistence & Privilege
dimensions.name: persistence_privilege

llm.guidance: Do not install or run this skill until the publisher clarifies several points: (1) why the skill uses two different domains (prana.chat and https://claw-uat.ebonex.io) to obtain and use API flags, and which service actually issues and receives the token; (2) why a persistent, global PRANA_SKILL_API_FLAG and gateway restart are required instead of a session-scoped token; (3) provide a homepage/source code or provenance so you can verify the publisher. If you must proceed, only use a scoped test account/token with minimal permissions, audit outbound requests, and avoid persisting credentials at system scope. Because the SKILL.md contains contradictory instructions (network_request headers vs curl examples) and asks you to write global env vars and restart services, treat it as suspicious until those inconsistencies are resolved.
